title: Define API/SDK model pin selector semantics (tag / semver / commit-hash) and performance-profile binding
creator: Avery Patel
description:
Goal: Define a clear, minimal, and backwards-compatible semantics for model selection/pinning exposed through the Redwood API and SDKs. The selector syntax must support three common primitives: human-friendly tags (e.g., 'stable', 'redwood/latest'), semantic versions (semver like '1.3.2' with optional ranges), and immutable commit hashes (git-like or model-build hashes).

This ticket captures the API surface, resolution precedence, runtime/compile-time guarantees, interactions with caching/response routing, and how a model's published performance profile (latency/cost/quality) is bound to a selector. The goal is to reduce unexpected runtime changes for customers and enable safe rollouts and automated fallbacks when models are unavailable or regress on quality metrics.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts a single 'model_selector' field that can be one of: tag:<name>, semver:<constraint>, or hash:<commit>. Examples documented in SDK README.
Resolution order specified and implemented: exact-hash > explicit-version > tag (with configurable tag policy per-tenant).
If a selector resolves to multiple model variants, resolution rules (highest stable semver, newest build) are deterministic and documented.
Performance profile binding: when a selector resolves we attach a performance_profile_reference that is immutable for that specific resolution and surfaced in response headers and console logs.
SDKs expose a 'resolve_before_send' opt-in flag for blocking resolution, and a non-blocking 'runtime_resolution' with documented fallback behavior.
Backward compatibility: existing 'model' field (legacy) accepts a string and resolves with the new semantics; behavior is covered with migration notes.
Integration tests for resolution precedence, cache key consistency, and fallback to compatible model variants exist in the runtime e2e suite.
Docs PR and changelog entry published with examples and recommended patterns for pinning in production (pin to hash for strict immutability; tag for progressive rollouts; semver for minor updates).
steps: Design selector grammar and validation rules in API layer (OpenAPI update + JSON Schema).
Implement resolver service: accept selector, return model_ref {model_id, build_hash, semver, perf_profile_id}. This is a server-side change in model-catalog service.
Add performance_profile_reference to runtime request context and include in metrics/traces and response headers (X-Redwood-Model-Profile).
SDK changes: parsing helpers, opt-in blocking resolution, and helper functions to build selectors from friendly inputs.
Add unit and e2e tests verifying cache keys contain resolved model build_hash to avoid cache poisoning across dynamic selectors.
Docs: examples, migration guide, and recommended patterns.
Rollout: feature-flagged server-side, enable SDK helpers in patch release, and collect telemetry for 2 weeks before default enabling.
decisions: Selectors are a single string field 'model_selector' to avoid proliferation of multiple overlapping fields.
We will normalize three canonical selector forms: 'tag:NAME', 'semver:CONSTRAINT', 'hash:HEX'. Freeform legacy names are allowed but deprecated.
Resolution precedence: hash (immutable) has highest precedence, semver exact match next, semver ranges next, then tag. Customers can opt into 'tag-stable-first' policy per org.

Performance profiles are versioned artifacts tied to resolved build_hash. A tag does NOT implicitly guarantee the same perf_profile over time; perf_profile_reference must be returned by the resolver and considered authoritative for the request.
SDKs will default to non-blocking runtime resolution to preserve low-latency paths, but expose blocking behavior for start-up or test scenarios.

When resolution fails, runtime falls back in order: pinned-compatible-variant (same family & quantization), org-default-model, then global-fallback-model. All fallbacks are logged and emitted as metrics.
Cache keys on inference servers include the resolved build_hash and perf_profile_id to ensure cache safety when tags move.
comments: 2025-02-11 - Avery Patel: Drafted selector grammar and initial precedence table; pairing with Diego for SDK ergonomics.
2025-02-18 - Diego Marquez: Implemented basic resolver prototype; confirmed resolver returns perf_profile_id. Need to wire into headers and telemetry.
2025-02-24 - Maya Chen (PM): Concern about customer surprise if tags are mutable; requested explicit migration guidance and org-level policies.
2025-02-27 - Security review request: noted that exposing build_hash is acceptable but we will not reveal internal S3 locations. Security OK-ed with audit logging requirement.
2025-03-01 - Design review (Lena Ortiz): Suggested changes to SDK helper naming and added examples for JS/Go.
notes: Key tradeoffs: strict immutability (hash pins) gives reproducibility but harms ability to opt-in to minor quality improvements; tags give operator ergonomics but require perf_profile binding and clear org policy to prevent silent regressions. We'll default to conservative behavior: expose perf_profile and require explicit org policy to treat tags as stable-mapping. SDK ergonomics prioritized: helper constructors for all selector types and defensive validation.
